newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 30.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The majority of economic experts in the Czech republic are expecting worse macroeconomic results in the coming year as compared with 1996. Neither expectations for inflation nor foreign trade are optimistic.
- While the crown strengthened on money markets during 1996, experts predict it will weaken in 1997.
- The cold weather in the last month of 1996 will not change estimated electricity usage, which is forecast to reach a record 55.3 terrawatt hours.

- Stock Plzen a.s., the largest domestic alcohol producer with approximately 23 percent market share, is expecting sales not including VAT to increase by a quarter over last year's 644 million crowns and net profit to increase by 12 percent over lasst year's 108 million crowns.

- Hard liquor producer Jan Becher - Karlovarska Becherovka posted the highest production in its 189-year history in 1996. Production has increased from 80,000 hectolitres in 1994 to 90,000 hectolitres in 1996, according to Ludmila Sulkova, an economist for the company.

- The majority of trade in industrial products between Israel and the Czech Republic will be duty free effective January 1, 1997 due to a free trade agreement. This is the first agreement of its type with a non-European country.

PRAVO - With investments in new technology amounting to 400 million crowns in 1996 alone, the Budejovicy Budvar n.p. brewery will begin gradually increasing its production capacity to up to 1.5 million hectolitres. This year's record output of 1.03 million hectolitres has resulted in sales increasing by approximately 230 million crowns. The gross profit will remain roughly the same as last year's 320 million crowns.
- Foresbank gained a majority of Podnikatelsky Penzijni Fond according to the general manager of the fund, Ludek Dytrych.
